subject: mathematics
concept: Understanding random sampling and why a sample should represent a larger population fairly
source_inspiration: adapted from NGSS-adjacent statistical reasoning principles — original content, not copied text

exercise.concrete: Student draws random samples from a physical population (colored counters) and compares sample results to the true population
exercise.pictorial: Student identifies which of several described sampling methods would produce a fair, representative sample
exercise.abstract: Student explains why a described sampling method is or isn't likely to be representative

misconception_flags: assumes any small sample, regardless of how it was selected, accurately represents the whole population

interest_binding: exercise regenerated using student's stated interest profile
